source.author: lucan
source.text: Ut vidit cominus enses, Involvit vultus, atque, indignatus apertum Fortunae praestare caput, tunc lumina pressit, Continuitque animam, ne quas effundere voces Posset, et aeternam fletu corrumpere tamam.
source.text_original: Ut vidit cominus enses, / Involvit vultus, atque, indignatus apertum / Fortunae praestare caput, tunc lumina pressit, / Continuitque animam, ne quas effundere voces / Posset, et aeternam fletu corrumpere tamam.
source.text_english: When he saw the swords close at hand, he covered his face, and, indignant to offer his bare head to Fortune, he then shut his eyes and held his breath, lest he might utter any words and mar his everlasting fame with tears.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: da, precor, amplexus haesuraque verba relinque auribus et dulci iam nunc preme lumina dextra.
reuse.text_original: da, precor, amplexus haesuraque verba relinque / auribus et dulci iam nunc preme lumina dextra.
reuse.text_english: Give me, I beg, your embrace, and leave your words to cling to my ears, and now at last close my eyes with your sweet right hand.
